summary: Scan for 2026-10-09 ended early because the search tool hit its usage limit after about 40 queries, almost all of them on the facepalm side. No facepalm candidate cleared every rule. The leads I found either have victims or injuries, are clerical or vendor errors like the ones already set aside, or are a single outlet's story republished by a sister station. I did not get to search the genius side. The earlier log shows the genius slot was already filled today (Deisseroth Nobel), and I found no other genius story to propose. Both sides are empty rather than risk an unverified story. No genius or facepalm story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: Louisville councilwoman apologizes for posting photo of wrong man in viral road-rage case
candidates.reason: A third party was harmed (an uninvolved man was publicly misidentified), and the underlying Sept. 30 fight left a woman injured. Fails the victim and injury exclusions.

candidates.headline: Second Louisville councilwoman says she 'overreacted' to road-rage video
candidates.reason: Tied to the same violent incident with an injured party. A statement walking back an earlier reaction is not a clear self-contained act.

candidates.headline: Maricopa County vendor mails 3,126 ballots a week early
candidates.reason: The county attributes it to an error by its printing vendor, a clerical mistake rather than a voluntary act, like the Oxford, Maine and Kendall County ballot stories already set aside. The 12News page could not be opened and KTAR is not on the accepted list, so only KJZZ was confirmed.

candidates.headline: Man arrested at Miami airport with 10 live birds in his underwear
candidates.reason: Live animals were sewn into tubes, so there are victims other than the perpetrator. The ABC11 page is a republished ABC News story (same canonical URL), so there is only one independent accepted publisher.

candidates.headline: Atlanta robbery suspect allegedly steals police cruiser and crashes into tanker truck
candidates.reason: The underlying robbery has a victim other than the perpetrator.
